subject: ventures/small-business-acquisition-calculator
professional: an SBA 7(a) acquisition loan officer / credit analyst (with the buyer-side M&A adviser who structures the same deal); first checks: is the amortisation right, how is DSCR defined (EBITDA vs SDE less replacement salary, which debt is in the denominator), does the 1.25 floor match SBA's change-of-ownership minimum, how a seller note on full standby is treated (SOP 50 10 8.1: no principal or interest for the whole 7(a) term, may accrue, counts for up to half of the equity injection), whether equity injection is measured on total project cost, and whether the SBA upfront guaranty fee is in the loan

evidence.correctness: Recomputed the sample deal with my own Python script (scratchpad sba-calc/indep.py; month-by-month schedule, bisection for max price, does not read calc.mjs) and compared with `node -e` on calc.mjs evaluate(sampleInputs()): bank DS 155,445.12 vs 155,445.12; seller DS 27,839.23 vs 27,839.23 (the published textbook payment for $100k/6%/5y is $1,933.28/mo, x1.2 = $2,319.94/mo = $27,839.28/yr); DSCR 1.3913 vs 1.3913 (standby 1.6405 vs 1.6405); bank balance after 60 months by explicit schedule 602,671.43 vs 602,671.43; max price at 1.25 by bisection 1,335,629.58 vs closed form 1,335,629.58; break-even SDE 288,284.35 (19.92% drop) vs same; after-debt 161,715.65, surplus 71,715.65, cash 218,000 all match. The arithmetic of every defined quantity is right. Not 4: with the standby box ticked the 'left after debt', surplus, return on cash and sensitivity cash rows still subtract the seller payments the SBA standby agreement forbids during the 7(a) term (surplus shown 71,716; year-one cash under standby is 99,555), and '90k' parses silently as 90.
evidence.completeness: README/page claims checked end to end via `node -e` and the served page (curl https://marisstella.app/small-business-acquisition-calculator/ -> 200, page text present): DSCR (works), cash needed at close incl. working capital (works), take-home after debt and after salary (works), highest price that clears the floor (works, lands exactly on 1.25), sensitivity table for -10/-20/-30% SDE (works), standby toggle (works as described), CSV report (works, test passes), notes for thin equity/high multiple/negative coverage (work). No stubs or TODOs. One dead output: bankBalance5 is computed and returned but never shown or tested. Things it says it does not do (valuation, lender rules, taxes) are listed under 'Not decided'.
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the venture: 27 tests pass, 0 fail. Seeded 5 mutants with quality_mutate.py on calc.mjs: monthly-rate divisor 12 -> 12.5 caught; afterDebt using DSCR debt instead of total debt caught; price/SDE warning threshold 4 -> 6 caught; sensitivity 'cash left after debt and your salary' with the salary deleted SURVIVED; return on cash computed on pre-salary cash flow SURVIVED. Two numbers shown to the user in the result tiles/table have no assertion. Tests are author-written and compare the code with its own formulas except the one $599.55 textbook payment check.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (133 lines), index.html (187), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, llms.txt, sitemap.xml. Small, pure, linear-in-price structure that makes the max-price closed form exact; escaping on the page; no network calls. Defects: num() uses parseFloat after stripping $ , % so '90k' -> 90 and '1.2M' -> 1.2 pass validation silently (calc.mjs:24); bankBalance5 dead (calc.mjs:103); footer boilerplate 'Not affiliated with any court, housing agency' copied from another venture and pinned by a test; no warning when the 'Bank / SBA' loan exceeds the $5M 7(a) maximum (a $7M deal gives a $5.6M bank loan and no note).
evidence.claims: Checked claims against files and SBA SOP 50 10 8.1 (effective 2026-10-01, downloaded from legacy.sba.gov). Backed: privacy/no-network (test), disclaimer and no-warranty footer, model and 'Not decided' list, 'lender practice was not checked with a lender' (honest), served llms.txt and sitemap carry https://marisstella.app/... (served-copy.mjs: no placeholder origin left). Not backed or wrong against the SOP: FAQ 'each lender sets its own floor' (App 15 sets a 1.25 minimum for Initial Acquisition and Owner Buyout); FAQ and note 'at least 10% of the price' (App 15: 10% of total project cost, cannot be waived for an Initial Acquisition, full-standby seller debt may supply up to half); FAQ standby 'no payments for some period' (only debt with no P&I for the whole 7(a) term counts as standby/equity); footer names courts and housing agencies.
evidence.fitness: Walked a buyer's first screen of a $1.2M listing with $360k SDE: the page answers 'does it clear 1.25, what cash do I need, how far can SDE fall' correctly and quickly, which is the job a searcher does before an LOI. An SBA loan officer would hit gaps in the first hour: no upfront guaranty fee financed into the loan (sample $25,200 = 3.5% x 75% x $960k, which raises the loan and debt service), no equity-injection test on total project cost with the standby-half rule, standby notes still drain year-one cash and accrue nothing, no 7(a) $5M cap or QoE >= $3M flag, pre-tax take-home only, one year only.
evidence.domain: Compared with SBA SOP 50 10 8.1 Appendix 15 and standard amortisation. Level monthly amortisation is right. DSCR as (SDE - replacement salary - capex) / post-transaction debt service is a defensible 'adjusted DSC' (App 15 allows adjustments for ownership compensation and unfunded capex; the historical DSC is EBITDA / combined debt service), and excluding a full-standby note from the denominator matches the SOP. Departures: standby treated as a 5-year amortising note paid from year one in cash flow, where the SOP requires no P&I for the full 7(a) term with interest allowed to accrue; equity measured on price, not total project cost, and standby debt's equity credit not modelled; floor input accepts 1.00-1.24 with a 'clears' verdict and no note that SBA's change-of-ownership minimum is 1.25; guaranty fee left to a cash '% of price' box.

defects.what: With 'full standby' ticked, cash flow after debt, surplus, return on cash and the sensitivity cash column still subtract the seller note's 5-year amortising payments from year one. Under SBA SOP 50 10 8.1 App 15 a full-standby note gets no principal or interest for the whole 7(a) term (it may accrue and amortise afterwards), so year-one take-home is understated (sample: shown $71,716, actual $99,555) while the later, larger payment on the accrued balance is not shown at all.

Two seeded mutants survive: removing the salary from the sensitivity table's 'cash left after debt and your salary' column, and computing return on cash on pre-salary cash flow. Both numbers are shown to the user and have no assertion.

SBA upfront guaranty fee is not modelled; the page tells users to type it into 'closing costs and loan fees, % of price (paid in cash)'. In a 7(a) acquisition it is a % of the guaranteed portion (SOP 50 10 8.1: 3.5% up to $1M guaranteed for $700k-$5M loans) and is usually financed, which raises the loan and debt service (sample $25,200).

Equity check and FAQ use '10% of the price'; SOP 50 10 8.1 App 15 requires 10% of total project cost for change of ownership (non-waivable for an Initial Acquisition) and lets full-standby seller debt supply up to half. The tool warns on a compliant 5% cash + 10% standby structure and never tests the standby-half rule.

FAQ says each lender sets its own DSCR floor; SOP 50 10 8.1 App 15 fixes a 1.25 minimum for Initial Acquisition and Owner Buyout. The floor input accepts 1.00-1.24 and reports 'clears' with no note; no warning when the 'Bank / SBA' loan exceeds the $5M 7(a) maximum or when price >= $3M triggers the QoE requirement.
num() strips $ , % and whitespace then uses parseFloat, so '90k' becomes 90 and '1.2M' becomes 1.2 and both pass validation silently.

FAQ describes standby as 'no payments for some period'; for SBA purposes only no-P&I for the full 7(a) term counts. Footer says 'Not affiliated with any court, housing agency' (boilerplate from another venture, pinned by page.test.mjs).
bankBalance5 is computed and returned but never displayed, exported or asserted beyond a loose bound.

verdict: The arithmetic is right: an independent Python recompute (month-by-month schedule, bisection) reproduces the sample deal to the cent, bank debt service 155,445.12, seller 27,839.23 (textbook $1,933.28/mo per $100k at 6%/5y), DSCR 1.3913 (1.6405 on standby), 60-month balance 602,671.43, max price at 1.25 1,335,629.58 and break-even SDE 288,284.35. Every claimed feature works and the served page and llms.txt are clean. It misses the bar on verification (2 of 5 seeded mutants survive, both on numbers shown to the user) and on claims and domain against SBA SOP 50 10 8.1 (effective 2026-10-01): standby notes still drain year-one cash although the SOP forbids any payment during the 7(a) term, equity is framed as 10% of price instead of total project cost with the standby-half rule, the 1.25 SBA minimum is described as lender choice and lower floors 'clear', and the upfront guaranty fee ($25,200 on the sample) is left to a cash box. A useful first screen for a buyer, not yet something an SBA loan officer would sign off.
